races.title: State House, District 74
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Jeff Zenger
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 74 (Forsyth County) since 2021. Contractor and small-business owner (Lisha Construction). Former Lewisville Planning Board chair and four-term Lewisville Town Council member. Lost the November 2026 general election to Amy Taylor North.
cands.gaps: We found no documented votes or sponsored bills we could read, so we can't show specific actions on any issue. The campaign site credits him with funding for four fire trucks, road improvements, the Shallow Ford park purchase and civil service protections for police and firefighters, but we found no official record confirming his role in these. We found no stated positions on data centers, development limits, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. We found no controversies or foreign ties. His exact birth year is not stated in the pages we read.

local.label: Roots 55: His campaign site says he was born in Washington, D.C., raised in Baltimore, and moved to Lewisville, NC in 1996, about 30 years ago as an adult (he graduated high school in 1982).

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since 2021, including as Finance Committee vice chair and Regulatory Reform chair. Before that he was Lewisville Planning Board chair and served four terms on the Lewisville Town Council. He has run a construction and development business since the late 1990s.
qual.why: Five years of state legislative service plus local elected office and a business-owner background fit the rubric's high band; committee posts were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: Five years of state legislative service plus local elected office and a business-owner background fit the rubric's high band; committee posts were not counted toward the score.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says he supports the Second Amendment and responsible gun ownership.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he will "back the blue" and lists support for law enforcement and first responders as a priority.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: His campaign site says he was born in Washington, D.C., raised in Baltimore, and moved to Lewisville, NC in 1996, about 30 years ago as an adult (he graduated high school in 1982).

cands.name: Amy Taylor North
cands.bio: Small business owner and communications specialist from Lewisville/Clemmons in Forsyth County. She created a national healthcare magazine in 2008 and volunteers in PTA and education work. She lost the 2024 race for NC House District 74 and won the 2026 rematch against incumbent Jeff Zenger.

endorsements.text: Candidate-listed endorsements include the NC Association of Educators, North Carolina Sierra Club, Lillian's List, EMILYs List, NC AFL-CIO and Carolina Federation.
Ballotpedia lists voter-guide recommendations from Work For Democracy and several Sway voting groups, including NC Public School Champions.
Anderson Clayton is quoted on her campaign site praising her ability to bring people together.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she grew up or the year she moved to North Carolina. We found no record of prior elected office or legislative work. We found no official actions such as bills sponsored or filings, so her positions come only from her own statements. Her campaign site mentions data centers as a strain on state resources and notes some strategic value in building them, but the page was cut off before any clear position, so none is reported. We found no stated position on homestead property taxes, limits on institutional or foreign land buyers, immigration enforcement, policing or gun policy.

local.label: Roots 40: She was born in Texas and graduated from Texas Tech in 1994, and her campaign says she has lived in Lewisville/Clemmons for over 20 years, which puts her move to North Carolina roughly 10-25 years ago.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Small business owner and communications specialist; created a national healthcare magazine in 2008; PTA and public-education volunteer. No prior elected office is documented.
qual.why: Business ownership places her in the middle band. No legislative service or law, policy or budget career was found.
qual.label: Business ownership places her in the middle band. No legislative service or law, policy or budget career was found.

pro-life.evidence: She says she supports reproductive rights, 'keeping politicians out of personal medical decisions' and restoring 'reproductive justice'.
